ashby:anrok:402c5d92-2dd6-4f82-91d5-fc36.summary:
Anrok is the leading tax automation platform enabling businesses to expand globally without compliance complexity.

As the digital economy has grown 6x over the last decade, software businesses have gone from not worrying about sales tax to needing to monitor exposure, calculate rates, and file returns across 20+ US states and many countries worldwide. This creates a critical bottleneck for companies that should be able to transact with customers everywhere.

Anrok eliminates this complexity by connecting with billing and payment systems to automate tax monitoring, calculations, and filing end-to-end. Our unified platform handles the ever-changing maze of tax laws at municipal, state, and federal levels—so companies can focus on growth, not compliance.

Manage a group of strategic contract renewals.

Collaborate with finance, customer solutions, and operations teams to ensure a seamless customer billing, expansion, and renewal experience.

ashby:assorthealth:57060bfc-6c78-447f-b7.summary:
Every time you call a doctor's office, the system forgets you the moment you hang up. You wait on hold, explain everything from scratch, get bounced between lines, and hope someone follows up. Everyone has felt this. No one should have to.

At Assort Health, we're building one continuous conversation for every patient. An AI agent that knows who you are, remembers how you like to be reached, and carries that context from your first symptom to your full recovery. What began as the first voice AI agent to schedule a specialty appointment has become the largest proprietary specialty dataset in healthcare: 345 million patient interactions, 62,000 care protocols, 1.6 million decision pathways.

Revenue is up 20x in 15 months and we've raised $222 million, including a recent $120 million Series C at a $1.2 billion valuation from investors including Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed. We've also been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 and the 2026 Enterprise Tech 30 as the only healthcare AI company on the list!
Healthcare spends $1.1 trillion a year on administration instead of care. If you want to help change that, apply below.

You will scope out new products and surface area end to end, leading the charge on new product workstreams 0→1. You’ll work directly with the CEO on a small yet quickly growing product team. Your work will directly improve healthcare access and the lives of both patients and providers.

bullets: Understand workflows, requirements, and bottlenecks
Design and present demos that showcase our capabilities
Collaborate with technical stakeholders to solve integration challenges

sections.title: Influence the Product Roadmap
paras: You’ll work with cross-functional partners to define requirements, prioritize features, and translate customer needs into actionable engineering work. You’ll help ensure we’re building the right capabilities at the right time to support our next phase of product growth: moving beyond just answering the phone.

We are launching proactive, agentic campaigns to close care gaps—reaching out to patients to schedule things like annual physicals and flu shots rather than waiting for them to react to health needs. We are also deploying Agent Memory to ensure every conversation feels personal. Our system uses past interactions to predict a patient’s needs: remembering if they prefer Spanish, adjusting speaking speed, or modulating voice tone to be more empathetic based on context.

But modern patient access isn’t just about voice. We are meeting patients where they are by expanding into chatbots and two-way texting. We are also fixing hidden friction in the background with our new referral orchestration and document processing platforms, ensuring that critical data is ingested automatically so patients get the care they need faster.

ashby:mindrobotics:a2b5ac83-e587-4c09-94.summary: Mind Robotics is building Physical AI for real-world industrial deployment, starting with the factory floor. We believe the hardest problems in AI are solved when researchers and engineers are hands-on with the physical world every day - and we're looking for people who are passionate about robotics, value ownership, and are excited to tackle difficult problems. Join us if you want to move beyond digital intelligence and put intelligence into motion.

sections.title: About the team and the role
paras: At Mind, we manufacture data. Every day our teams produce the robot training data our foundation models learn from, much as a factory produces parts. Teleoperators drive our robots through real manufacturing tasks at our Palo Alto HQ, field technicians capture data on customer factory floors, and third-party partners deliver datasets we buy. Everyone on the team thinks about data quality every day. But as in any manufacturing operation, quality is too important to leave to each production line on its own. It needs one owner who sees across all of them and holds every source to a common standard.

As Data Quality Lead, you will be that owner. You will build Mind's new Data Quality function and report directly to Daniel Burrows, Head of Data. You will set a single quality standard across our three data sources: third-party data, teleoperation and field data collection. You will define what "good data" means with our research teams, build the inspection and measurement systems that check it, trace defects to their root cause, and make sure every hour of data that reaches training meets the bar. This is a rare chance to build the quality system for a new kind of manufacturing, where the product is the data that teaches robots to work.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Define the quality standard. With research and data infrastructure, write and maintain one versioned quality specification for all data sources, covering sensor synchronization and calibration, frame rates and dropouts, episode completeness, task success, labeling accuracy, metadata, and coverage of tasks, embodiments and environments.

Build inspection into every stage. Design automated checks and sampling-based human review from capture through ingestion to training-ready datasets: incoming inspection for vendor deliveries, in-line checks on the teleoperation floor and at field sites, and final acceptance before data enters a training set.

Measure quality like a factory. Own quality metrics for each source and in total, such as usable-hour yield, defect rates by type, first-pass acceptance, rework and rejection rates, and cost of poor quality. Publish a quality dashboard and run a weekly quality review.

Run root cause and corrective action. When defects appear, trace them to their source (operator technique, rig or sensor faults, software, vendor processes or labeling guidelines), drive corrective and preventive actions with the owning team, and confirm the fix holds.

Hold third-party data to the same bar. With Data Strategy, set quality acceptance criteria and SLAs for vendor contracts, run incoming inspection and pilot audits, and feed quality scores into vendor reviews, renewals and exits.

Build quality in at the source. Work with the Teleoperations and Field Data Collection leads to build quality into operator training, task setups, rigs and collection procedures, so fewer defects are created in the first place.

Connect data quality to model performance. Work with researchers to learn which defects actually hurt policy learning, prioritize fixes by their impact on models, and update the specification as tasks and models change.
Raise labeling quality. With Annotation & Labelling, set label QA processes, calibration sets and inter-annotator agreement targets, and fold label quality into the same standard as raw data.

sections.title: Requirements
bullets: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a closely related quantitative field, or equivalent experience.
6+ years in quality engineering, data quality or data operations. Owning quality for ML training data, sensor data or a manufacturing process is a plus.

Hands-on experience with quality management methods such as statistical process control, sampling plans, root cause analysis (5 Whys, fishbone, 8D) and corrective and preventive action (CAPA). Six Sigma or a similar certification is a plus.
Fluency in Python and SQL sufficient to build checks, analyze datasets and own quality metrics yourself.
Experience setting quality requirements for, and auditing, external vendors or suppliers.
Experience working with ML researchers or engineers on how data quality affects model performance is a plus.
Ability to drive change across teams without direct authority, with clear, data-driven written and verbal communication.
Able to work at our Palo Alto HQ, with occasional travel to field collection sites and vendors.

ashby:speak:63a85014-658d-4612-b438-2d3b.summary:
Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders…

sections.title: About this role
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to answer a question every learner and customer should be able to answer: is the learner actually getting better?

Speak sees many signals of progress — assessments, practice, mistakes, learning activity, and what a learner can do over time. Today, those signals do not yet form one clear picture. This PM will turn them into a product that helps learners understand where they are, whether they are improving, and what to do next. For companies using Speak, the same work should provide credible evidence that their learners are making progress.

This is a hands-on senior IC role. You'll work across Product, Engineering, Analytics, Learning, Design, and our B2B team, but the job is not to coordinate those groups. The job is to learn the problem deeply, make the product choices, and ship.

sections.title: What you'll be doing
bullets: Own product strategy and roadmap for learning outcomes and proficiency.
Talk directly with learners and B2B customers to understand how they judge progress today and where the current experience fails them.
Decide which signals of proficiency and progress are trustworthy enough to drive product decisions.
Ship improvements in assessment, progress, and feedback that help learners understand where they are and what to do next.
Connect measurement back to the learning experience so what we know about a learner changes what Speak does for them.
Define practical quality bars for accuracy, trust, transparency, and actionability.
Work with Engineering, Analytics, Learning, and Design to turn ambiguous evidence into a focused product decision and a measured release.

sections.title: What we're looking for
paras: If you don't think you meet every criterion below but are excited about the role, please apply. We care more about evidence of strong product judgment and learning speed than a perfect match on background.

sections.title: Must-have Qualifications
bullets: Strong product judgment in ambiguous, 0→1 problems: you can choose what matters, narrow scope, and explain what you would learn next.
Experience combining user research and product data to make consequential product decisions.
Systems thinking: you can understand how user experience, data, models, workflows, and technical constraints fit together without losing sight of the user problem.
A track record of shipping products with measurable user or business outcomes.
Clear written and verbal communication.

paras:
As a Senior Value Engineer specializing in the Public Sector, you are pushing the envelope in solving critical operational challenges for State and Local Government agencies. You will prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to government CIOs and Agency Directors, and ensure successful implementation, adoption, and value realization to increase the footprint of Celonis across state and local governments.

sections.title: Our Guiding Principles
bullets: Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don’t hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.

Help Customers Win. We learn our customers’ businesses deeply: how they think, how they deploy capital, and what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features, and measure ourselves by customer results.
Move with Urgency and Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds, and we build it every day.
Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it.
Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and change our minds when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

Kapitus is building a next-generation enterprise data and AI capability that replaces hundreds of legacy analytics workflows with governed, reusable business data products — moving the organization from producing reports to producing decisions.

As a Data Product Lead, you own data products through their full life cycle — from business problem and value hypothesis, through business case, build, launch, adoption, and usage reporting, to retirement of products and the legacy reports they replace. You are the bridge between business requirements, data engineering, governance, and customer-facing teams, and you manage products against outcomes business leaders recognize, not technical output.

This is a product-discipline role, not a hands-on engineering role. You must understand our architecture well enough to link requirements to it and hold credible conversations with engineers. Experience in our business vertical is required, not preferred: you will not be learning the language of lending on the job. AI fluency is an advantage, not a requirement.
bullets: Identify business problems worth solving with data; clarify each product's value proposition — utility, decision enabler, or driver of new business value — and quantify expected impact before anything is built.
Own usage reporting and portfolio transparency: scorecards, value stories co-created with stakeholders, and regular reviews informing invest, pivot, or retire decisions.
Own retirement: sunset policies, end-of-life roadmaps, and structured decommissioning for products — and legacy workflows — that fail to sustain business value.

Elicit requirements through stakeholder interviews, focus groups, and customer journey mapping; translate vague, ill-defined needs into well-defined, testable product requirements with clear acceptance criteria.
Turn requirements into product definitions engineering can build: named owners, defined consumers, data contracts, certified semantic definitions, quality thresholds, and service levels.

Link every requirement to our platform architecture — layered data foundation, governed core entities, certified semantics, and serving channels (BI, APIs, ML, AI) — so products are built on the platform, not beside it.
Champion prototyping and iteration: confirm value with consumers at every development stage rather than specifying once and walking away.
Serve as the connective tissue between business requirements, data engineering, governance, and customer-facing teams, translating in both directions so needs and delivery stay aligned.

paras: The Manager of Finance Integration owns the finance and accounting workstream across Orion's acquisitions, from late stage diligence through the first close cycles under our ownership. This role sits on the Corporate Controllership team and reports to the VP, Corporate Controller.

You will serve two very different clients. Before close, you support the deal team: pressure-testing the quality of earnings and forming a view on the accounting, tax, legal, and back-office exposure that transaction diligence does not always reach. After close, your client becomes the finance team of the company we just bought. You are on the ground with them, standing up the opening balance sheet, converting their accounting onto our processes and lead schedules, and getting them audit ready alongside the rest of the network.

This is a builder’s role. Our Group VPs of Finance lead the effort to bring each acquisition in their region up to the Orion standard. You build and implement the frameworks and playbooks that make that possible and carry them from deal to deal. You will work alongside the M&A Integrations Manager, who runs the overall integration program, while you own the finance workstream inside it. Much of the value here comes from being physically present at newly acquired companies, working shoulder to shoulder with a controller who has never operated inside a platform before.

Documentation discipline - you maintain and improve the frameworks and templates that let other people repeat what you did, written well enough to execute without you in the room.

Prolaio believes that continuous learning and collaboration can make a significant difference in how heart care is administered. We are creating smarter ways to address heart disease and heart risks by uniting patients, care teams, and researchers on a secure, technology-enabled platform that drives clinical innovation and offers a path towards better patient outcomes.

This is precision cardiology, and we know it’s within reach.

sections.title: The Overview
paras: The Implementation Engineer owns the technical configuration of every Prolaio clinical trial instance, from protocol handoff to go-live and through mid-study amendments. This role translates protocol and sponsor requirements into a working, validated platform configuration: sites, devices, participant workflows, alerts, and data flows. The Implementation Engineer executes and documents User Acceptance Testing, produces the screenshots and system documentation required for IRB and ethics submissions, and serves as the operational team's first line of technical troubleshooting. The role sits in Operations but works daily with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Clinical Services so that studies launch on time, configured correctly, and inspection-ready.

sections.title: The Specifics
bullets: Configure clinical trial instances end to end from the protocol, Statement of Work, and configuration specification: study and site setup, user roles and access, device assignments, participant workflows, schedules of assessments, alert and notification rules, and data export settings.
Author and maintain configuration specifications and change logs for each study, ensuring the configured system traces back to approved requirements.
Plan, write, and execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) scripts; document results, log and track defects to resolution, and obtain UAT sign-off before go-live and after every configuration change.

Produce IRB and ethics submission packages for participant-facing materials, including annotated app and portal screenshots, screen flows, and system descriptions, and turn around revisions requested by sponsors, CROs, or review boards.
Manage protocol amendments and mid-study configuration changes under change control, including impact assessment, re-testing, and re-submission support.

Serve as Tier 2 technical support for the Help Desk and Clinical Services: troubleshoot configuration, device pairing, data sync, and integration issues; escalate product defects to Engineering with clear reproduction steps.
Coordinate with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Platform Architecture on release impacts, new feature configuration, and data pipeline setup for each study.
Support site and sponsor onboarding with technical walkthroughs, environment demos, and configuration-related training materials.

sections.title: Why Prolaio?

Innovative Environment : You will be part of an organization doing something that’s never been done before.
Professional Growth : You will join a growing team and have a substantial impact on our daily and future operations with the opportunity to continuously learn and grow.

Collaborative Team : You will be part of a team of collaborative, curious, and committed individuals focused on the collective good, inclusiveness, scientific excellence, and advancing digital health for cardiology.

3–5 years configuring, implementing, or supporting software platforms, with at least 2 years in clinical trial technology such as eCOA/ePRO, EDC, IRT, RTSM, or remote patient monitoring systems.
Hands-on experience writing and executing UAT or validation test scripts and documenting results in a regulated environment.
Working knowledge of GCP, 21 CFR Part 11, and computer system validation principles; familiarity with IRB submission requirements for participant-facing technology.
Strong technical troubleshooting skills across web portals, mobile apps, and connected devices, including reading logs and isolating configuration versus software defects.
Clear, precise technical writing; able to produce specifications, test evidence, and submission-ready documentation that holds up to sponsor and auditor review.
Comfortable managing several concurrent study builds with fixed go-live dates, and working directly with sponsors, CROs, and sites.

sections.title: The Role
paras: Extreme Networks is building the next generation of autonomous cloud networking platforms for the enterprise. sections.title: How Enterprise Operations Are Evolving
paras: Enterprise networks are moving from fully manual operations toward a hybrid model in which teams continue to operate the network while autonomous agents handle specific, scoped tasks.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager to own Identity & Access Management (IAM) as a platform service—not simply as a feature backlog. In this role, you will define the architecture, governance model, and roadmap for identity across Extreme Platform ONE as enterprise customers expand their networks to support autonomous agents.The operating model is intentionally built for both human operators and autonomous agents. Humans remain in control of judgment-driven work, governance, and exception handling, while agents take on well-defined, repetitive tasks such as health monitoring, standard deployments, and routine optimizations.

This is a highly cross-functional, high-visibility role at the intersection of platform strategy, customer success, AI innovation, and service ownership across networking and security. You will partner closely with platform service owners, engineering leaders, and executive stakeholders to support a broad set of enterprise use cases.
bullets: Human identity supports sessions, interactive workflows, and judgment-driven decisions such as policy changes, architecture updates, and incident response.

Agent identity enables 24/7 autonomous execution for routine, well-defined work—but only within explicit boundaries. Agents can operate independently when the task is in scope, and must escalate exceptions, anomalies, or boundary violations to humans.

sections.title: How We Work — please read this part carefully
paras: This role works differently from most product jobs, and the difference matters more than anything else on this page.

Ali, our founder and CEO, sets company priorities. You own the ideas. You will own an app or area end to end, and you will spend part of every day researching competitors, the industry and our users to generate new feature ideas. Every product manager here keeps a live Top 3 list of the highest-impact ideas for their area — a new idea only enters that list by beating one already on it.

You pitch ideas to Ali on a single slide with a rough impact calculation attached. He rejects the ones that will not move the number enough to justify building them. That happens often, to everyone, and it is not a signal that anything has gone wrong.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Own an app or area end to end — the roadmap, the backlog, the revenue and retention of it
Generate the ideas. Research competitors, the market and our users daily, and keep a ranked Top 3 that you are constantly trying to beat
Build the impact case before you build the feature: size the opportunity, show the maths, defend the number
Pitch to Ali, take the rejection, sharpen it, come back
Drive approved work through spec, design, engineering, QA and launch
Design and run A/B tests, ramp them responsibly, and read the results honestly — including when you lost
Publish what you learn, wins and losses alike, to the whole company
Hit the impact you predicted

Evidence you have moved toward the product rather than the title — a lateral or downward title move to get closer to building something, or two or three functions inside one company.
Something you started that nobody asked you to start. A side project, a club, a process, a business, a team you created because it needed to exist.

paras: At Signode, we recognize and reward talent. This role offers a competitive annual salary plus a Sales Incentive Plan and varies based on specific responsibilities and geographic location. The starting annual salary will be determined based on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and/or skillset.

sections.title: Summary:
paras: The Enterprise Account Manager is responsible for cultivating and managing strategic relationships with high-value national clients. This role focuses on driving account growth through both retention and expansion initiatives. The consultant engages with key decision-makers across all levels of customer organizations. Accounts managed are national in scope and must demonstrate potential for comprehensive product adoption.
Looking for candidates located in: Detroit, MI, Atlanta, GA, Dallas, TX, Denver, CO, Salt Lake City, UT, or Minneapolis, MN

sections.title: Essential Functions:
bullets: Create and identify opportunities in assigned accounts and develop strategies / account plans to execute against opportunities.
Leads relationship and adoption activities for accounts that are landed by the Business Development Executive.
Meet or exceed assigned sales goals .
Acts as a main point of contact with customers regarding ongoing business requirements and issues.
Develop strong business relationships at key accounts, culminating in Joint Business Plans (JBPs) with top volume customers.
Penetrate all levels of assigned accounts through multiple departments (i.e. executives, buying, logistics, service and replenishment).
Resolves customer inquiries, problems, and complaints to maximize customer satisfaction.
Creates account plans and identifies expansion opportunities.

sections.title: Education:
paras: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, Finance or similar field.
